headline: A 3.7 percent US September CPI print turned the Oct 28 Fed meeting from a hold into a live hike debate, knocking the Nasdaq Composite down 1.88 percent, silver down 4.79 percent and Oracle down 8.83 percent while CoreWeave's 2032 bond yield touched 15 percent, and the selling has carried into Thursday's Asia session with the Kospi down 7.18 percent and Samsung Electronics down 8.3 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Wednesday at 7,718.94, down 1.11 percent, the Nasdaq Composite at 26,692.87, down 1.88 percent, and the Dow at 51,621.48, down 0.09 percent, after September CPI printed 3.7 percent on the year against a 3.6 percent consensus, core at 2.6 percent against 2.5 percent, and gasoline up 9.1 percent accounting for about half the monthly gain, which moved futures pricing at the Oct 28 Fed meeting from a hold toward a hike. The second blow came from AI credit, with CoreWeave's 2032 bond yield touching 15 percent before settling near 14.5 percent, the yield on Oracle's 6.25 percent 2032 notes at 7.24 percent, Oracle down 8.83 percent to 130.55 dollars, Dell down about 11 percent on a Barclays downgrade and the VIX up 10.48 percent to 16.87, while JPMorgan rose 1.16 percent the day after a rare revenue miss alongside a Goldman Sachs beat.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed Wednesday at 22,622.70, down 0.44 percent, and Bank Nifty at 55,316, down 0.30 percent, with foreign investors net sellers of about 1,857 crore rupees in the cash segment against domestic buying of about 2,670 crore rupees, a fourteenth straight session of FII selling, and crude near 94 dollars weighing on sentiment. Nifty IT was the exception at up 1.14 percent after HCLTech lifted its FY27 constant currency growth guidance to 2.5 to 4 percent from 1 to 4 percent, while non bank lenders fell after the RBI raised the daily cash reserve ratio maintenance requirement to 99 percent of the prescribed level from 90 percent, a change Jefferies estimated could absorb 400 billion to 800 billion rupees, and the rupee closed near 95.16 per dollar as Governor Sanjay Malhotra restricted rebooking of cancelled forex derivative contracts.
summary.global: Thursday's Asia session extended the memory selloff that began when China's CXMT described a denser 4F squared DRAM design at a Shanghai conference on Oct 10, with the Kospi down 7.18 percent to 5,577.32, Samsung Electronics down 8.3 percent, the Nikkei 225 down 4.03 percent to 65,015.37 and Taiwan down 2.59 percent, and CNBC tying Thursday's leg to worries that higher borrowing costs squeeze AI infrastructure spending. Europe had moved the other way on Wednesday, with the FTSE 100 up 0.70 percent at 10,724.90 and the DAX up 0.15 percent after ASML guided fourth quarter sales above consensus and reported customers booking tools for 2029 and 2030, while Brent held near 105 to 108 dollars and WTI near 94 dollars after a cargo ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz, set against OPEC+ September output up about 900,000 barrels a day.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
